meta.description: AI agents: landscape and how they work

user.t:
READ-ONLY research. Use WebSearch/WebFetch; cite sources with dates. Write to C:\Users\mariu\AppData\Local\Temp\claude\C--Users-mariu\8f3352b3-40ab-4151-abc9-d1de1978973c\scratchpad\agents-landscape.md and return a concise summary. No installs, no MCP, no code changes.

Topic: how TODAY's AI agents actually work, are built, and are researched. Cover, with citations and honest "verified vs hyped" tags:
1. Architecture: LLM core + tool use + memory/RAG + planning/orchestration + multi-agent patterns; the frontier agent products and frameworks (e.g. Claude/Agent SDK, OpenAI, LangGraph, AutoGen, CrewAI, etc.).
2. How they're built and improved in practice (scaffolding, context engineering, tool design, evals).
3. How they're researched/measured: key benchmarks (SWE-bench, GAIA, WebArena, tau-bench, etc.), what scores actually mean, and current real-world capability AND limits (reliability, long-horizon, hallucination, cost/latency).
4. What is genuinely hard/unsolved. Be blunt about hype vs evidence.
Honest frame: the "intelligence" is a frozen LLM; agent gains come from scaffolding/tools/memory/verification, not magic. No claims of a startup being able to out-model frontier labs.

handback.t:
Wrote C:\Users\mariu\AppData\Local\Temp\claude\C--Users-mariu\8f3352b3-40ab-4151-abc9-d1de1978973c\scratchpad\agents-landscape.md. It has cited sources with [V]/[S]/[H] tags. Some sources were unreadable (OpenAI's SWE-bench post returned 403, morphllm returned 429), and several numbers below come from secondary summaries. Those are tagged [S] in the file.

**Summary**

1. **Architecture**
   - An agent is a frozen LLM in a loop with tools. Memory is the context window plus external notes plus retrieval; planning is the model's own reasoning.
   - Anthropic's own split is workflows (fixed code paths) vs agents (the LLM directs its own process). Agents cost more and compound errors. [V]
   - Multi-agent systems mostly buy parallelism and context isolation.
     - Anthropic's research system reportedly beat a single agent by 90% at about 15x the tokens, and token usage explained about 80% of the variance. [S]
     - Cognition argues for single-threaded agents with strong context engineering. [opinion, not a measurement]
     - The MAST study of 1,642 traces found failure rates of 41-87%, driven mostly by loose specs, misalignment between agents, and weak verification. [S]
   - MCP and AGENTS.md now sit under the Linux Foundation's Agentic AI Foundation, backed by Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, Microsoft and AWS. [V]
   - Framework comparison blogs are low quality. LangGraph is the production-oriented choice, CrewAI is easiest to prototype with, and the vendor SDKs are the Claude Agent SDK, OpenAI Agents SDK and Google ADK. I did not verify the AutoGen-to-Microsoft Agent Framework status.

2. **How agents are built and improved**
   - Context engineering is the main craft: compaction, note-taking to external memory, subagents with clean contexts, just-in-time retrieval, and "context rot" as the problem being managed. [V, Anthropic, 2025-09-29]
   - Tool design matters: clear formats, documented edge cases, tested with real model runs, and parameters that make misuse hard. [V]
   - Scaffold effects are large. Opus 4.5 scored 45.9% on SWE-bench Pro under a standardized scaffold and 55.4% under Claude Code. HAL reports double-digit gaps from harness alone, and token use can swing about 65x. [S]
   - Verification loops (tests, independent reviewers) and evals that grade on pass^k rather than pass@1 are the reliable levers.

3. **Measurement**
   - SWE-bench Verified is saturated and contaminated. OpenAI stopped reporting it in early 2026 and recommends SWE-bench Pro. [S]
   - tau-bench: GPT-4-class agents got under 50% on a single run and about 25% when the same task was repeated 8 times. [V]
   - Benchmarks vary by harness:
     - GAIA: humans about 92%, top about 75% with scaffolding vs 45% bare. [S]
     - WebArena: about 72% against a human baseline of about 78%. [S]
     - OSWorld: reported in the mid-80s against a human 72%. These are system submissions (model plus harness plus retries), not raw model skill. [S]
   - METR time horizon (TH1.1, Jan 2026): Opus 4.5 about 320 minutes at 50% success, GPT-5 about 214. Doubling time was about 7 months over 2019-2025 and about 4 months since 2024. METR itself caveats that only 5 of 31 long tasks have measured human baselines and that the suite is near saturation. [V]
   - Remote Labor Index (real freelance projects): best agent about 2.5% automation in Oct 2025. [S]
   - METR's RCT found developers 19% slower while believing they were 20% faster. A 2026 follow-up was inconclusive (CI -38% to +9%). [V / S]
   - Gartner forecasts over 40% of agentic projects canceled by end of 2027, with "agent washing" among vendors. That is a forecast, not an outcome. [V]

4. **Hard and unsolved**
   - Reliability and consistency across repeated runs, and errors compounding over long tasks.
   - Context rot and drift; memory is just files and retrieval because the weights are frozen.
   - Agents claiming success without verification.
   - Cost: multi-agent runs use about 15x the tokens.
   - Prompt injection: AgentDojo attack success is around 21% on average, and restricting tools before the agent sees untrusted data cut targeted success from 58% to 7%. [S] The "lethal trifecta" is private data plus untrusted content plus external communication.
   - Contaminated, saturated and scaffold-dependent benchmarks, and multi-agent coordination failures.

5. **Honest frame**
   - The intelligence is the frozen LLM; the real value is scaffolding, tool design, context management, verification, evals, and human-in-the-loop design.
   - Lab model gains and lab-built harnesses can erode scaffold-only advantages, so a startup cannot out-model the frontier labs. It can compete on domain integration, verification, trust and distribution.
   - Hype to discount: leaderboard numbers with no harness or cost disclosure, "autonomous employee" and swarm marketing, vendor-reported multi-agent gains, and "self-improving" agents (I found no verified evidence).

**Not verified:**
- Current tau2-bench and SWE-bench Pro top scores.
- AutoGen/Agent Framework status.
- Hallucination rates and 2026 pricing.
- OpenAI's own SWE-bench post (403; I relied on search snippets and an OpenAI X post).
- Some model names in leaderboard snippets, which I could not confirm.
